title: add nvtx counters, microbench instrumentation, and perf dashboard
author: Leah Chen
description: Context: We need better visibility into per-kernel latency and scheduling behavior in the serving runtime to diagnose tail latency and regression risk when changing kernels, batching, or KV cache logic. This PR adds NVTX ranges and lightweight counters around key runtime hotspots (kernel dispatch, KV cache hits/misses, continuous-batching enqueue/dequeue, request serialization), a microbenchmark harness for deterministic kernel and batching microbenchmarks, and an initial Grafana dashboard + derived metrics to surface distributions and regression alerts. Motivation: recent perf regressions were hard to triage in prod due to lack of fine-grained timeline and counter visibility. This change is aimed at making microbench results and production traces comparable and enabling faster root cause analysis when we change kernel selection or scheduling heuristics. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a small instrumentation API (runtime/include/instrumentation.h) and NVTX wrappers (runtime/profiler/nvtx_wrappers.{cpp,cu}) that add annotated NVTX ranges around: kernel_launch, kernel_execute, kv_cache_read, kv_cache_write, batch_enqueue, batch_dequeue, trace_serialize. NVTX calls are guarded behind a runtime flag (--enable-instrumentation) and compiled out when DISABLE_INSTRUMENTATION is defined to avoid steady-state overhead. 2) Adds atomic counters (runtime/profiler/counters.cc) exported to the observability registry (prometheus-style) for key events: kernel_invoke_total, kv_cache_hit_total, kv_cache_miss_total, batching_enqueue_total, batching_dequeue_total, batch_size_histogram. 3) Adds a deterministic microbench harness (tools/microbench/) with workloads for kernel latency, kv-cache lookup, and batching steady-state throughput. The harness runs kernels with controlled sequence lengths and batch sizes and emits both NVTX traces and counter snapshots. 4) Adds Grafana dashboard JSON (observability/grafana/runtime_profiling_dashboard.json) with panels for per-kernel p50/p95/p99, queue length, cache hit ratio over time, and a waterfall view keyed by NVTX ranges. The dashboard includes alert thresholds for sudden increases in p95 kernel latency and drops in cache hit ratio. 5) CI integration: new perf job (ci/perf-pipeline.yaml) that can run microbench workloads in GPU testbed; perf job gated behind a pipeline variable to avoid slowing every PR. 6) Docs: docs/perf/instrumentation.md describing how to run microbenches, interpret NVTX traces (with Nsight Systems), and add dashboard panels. Checklist: - [x] NVTX wrappers and range annotations added - [x] Counters exported to metrics registry - [x] Microbench harness with seedable workloads - [x] Grafana dashboard initial version - [x] CI perf job (optional trigger) - [x] Unit tests + integration microbench smoke test - [x] Docs updated Rollout: instrumentation is opt-in by default (flag off). We will enable on canary nodes for 48h and verify no measurable overhead on P50/P95 in canary before wider rollout. Related: ENG-1824 (kernel selection telemetry), ENG-1837 (batching regression alerting).

review_comments: Marco Silva: Nice work. Two asks before merge: 1) quantify the NVTX runtime overhead in a microbench (p50/p95) and 2) ensure metric names follow our naming conventions (dot vs underscore).

Leah Chen (author): Added a microbench run in the PR and included a short table in the docs showing <0.5% p50 overhead with NVTX disabled by default; switched metric names to use underscores per convention.
Diana Ortiz: Please add labels to kernel_invoke_total for model and device to make it sliceable in dashboards.
Leah Chen (author): counters.cc now attaches labels {model, device} where available; for older callers the labels are empty strings to avoid label cardinality explosion.
Jin Park: CI perf job initially failed on GPU runner (OOM on synthetic workload). Can we add a smaller default workload and a heavyweight mode?
Leah Chen (author): Added two modes to microbench (smoke and heavy). CI uses smoke by default; heavy can be run manually in testbed. Ran heavy locally on our x2 machine and adjusted memory footprint.
Marco Silva: Approved after verifying perf job passed on canary and metrics naming/labels fixed.
Diana Ortiz: LGTM. Merging when CI green.

release_notes: Add optional runtime NVTX instrumentation and counters, microbench harness, and an initial runtime profiling Grafana dashboard. Instrumentation is opt-in and guarded to avoid steady-state overhead. Useful for diagnosing kernel and batching regressions.
summary_of_changes: Adds opt-in NVTX range annotations around kernel and batching hotspots, lightweight counters exported to metrics registry, a microbench harness for deterministic kernel/batching workloads, a Grafana dashboard for kernel latency and cache metrics, CI perf job integration, and docs explaining usage and overhead expectations.
motivation: Improve observability of kernel, KV cache, and batching behavior to accelerate debugging of latency regressions and to provide stable baselines for optimizer changes.
testing_notes: Microbench smoke tests run in CI (GPU). Heavy workloads run manually in the GPU testbed. Nsight Systems traces can be produced by running the microbench with --nvtx and analyzed with the provided dashboard mappings. Performance regressions should be validated on canary nodes with flag enabled for 48h.
notes_for_ops: Instrumentation is off by default. Enable via runtime flag --enable-instrumentation on canary nodes only. Counters are low overhead and exposed to Prometheus; ensure Prometheus scrape target is configured for new metrics. The Grafana dashboard uses labels {model,device} to slice data.
